Build a grounded AI agent with Azure HorizonDB

Your agent is only as good as the data behind it. Join us to build a working agent that retrieves trusted context from operational PostgreSQL data in Azure HorizonDB. Create an AI pipeline, generate embeddings, combine vector and keyword retrieval, apply filters, and connect results to an agent workflow. Leave with a reusable architecture and working implementation.

embeddingContent: Build a multi-agent team with Microsoft Foundry and AMD GPUs Utilize open-weight models from Microsoft Foundry on AMD GPUs to build a team of AI agents. Start with one OpenClaw agent, explore the files that give it memory and behavior, and use it to find a bug in a live Python environment. Then build a team of specialists working in parallel, with a coordinator that delegates tasks to resolve the bug. Finish with a challenge to add a new agent and tackle a new problem. Beginner friendly, with no prior agent experience required.

embeddingContent:
Build agentic document workflows with Content Understanding

Enterprise processes start with unstructured content—documents, images, audio, video, emails. Before AI agents can act, they must understand and structure it. In this hands-on lab, use Azure Content Understanding (CLI, SDKs) in an agent loop to build an end-to-end workflow. Process real business content, extract and classify information, and route work through automated decision paths. Learn confidence-based automation and human-in-the-loop review for straight-through processing.

embeddingContent: Build local AI agents on AMD Ryzen AI PCs An always-on agent is only worth having if you can trust it with real work. In this hands-on lab, you'll build an agent on an AMD Ryzen™ AI PC and define what it can access and do. Use Lemonade Server to keep model calls local across the NPU and GPU, and Microsoft MXC to run the agent in a sandbox with policies you control. You'll use a synthetic dataset and simulated environment to build and experiment with a fun productivity use case.

Deploy and operate AI inference on AKS without building a cluster from scratch. Deploy a prepared AI application to AKS Automatic, request GPU resources, and watch Automatic provision the required compute. embeddingContent:
Delegate complex work: Hands-on with Copilot Cowork

Agent usage is up 15× year over year, and more multi-step workflows can now be delegated end to end. In this hands-on session, build a real workflow with Copilot Cowork: turn a complex process into a skill, extend it with plugins and automations, and see how Cowork plans, executes, and delivers work across systems and apps. Leave with a publishable skill and a practical model for deciding what to delegate, how to scope it, and how to move work from intent to done.

embeddingContent:
Design multi-model routing for AI efficiency with NVIDIA Switchyard

Modern AI applications demand flexibility because different tasks require different models. In this hands-on lab, deploy NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard, an open-source LLM traffic router, on Azure with Microsoft Foundry. Switchyard's stage-based routing directs each request to the right model, escalating to a more capable one only when needed, without changing your application code. Walk away with a multi-model strategy you can apply to your own AI workloads.

Ground agents in your business with an ontology in Fabric IQ

Learn how to build, govern, and share business context with Fabric IQ. In this hands-on lab, you'll create an ontology from Power BI semantic models and OneLake data, define business concepts and relationships using Copilot, and publish reusable intelligence across teams. See how OneLake sharing extends governed semantic models and ontologies beyond organizational boundaries, helping AI agents, analytics, and applications reason from a common understanding of the business.

embeddingContent:
Hands-on with the resiliency in Azure: Assess, recommend, recover

In this hands-on lab, experience Azure resiliency across availability, disaster recovery, data resiliency, and cyber recovery. Define resiliency goals for a sample workload, assess readiness against zonal and regional failures, identify gaps against RTO/RPO targets, and apply guided recommendations to improve resiliency. Perform clean-room recovery to restore trusted data after an attack and leave with a practical, repeatable approach using Azure resiliency capabilities and AI-assisted guidance.

Hands-on: Modernize apps and databases and automate operations

Get hands-on using AI to modernize applications, databases, and operations. Use GitHub Copilot to assess and upgrade a Java or .NET app, remediate dependencies, containerize workloads, and modernize the database. Then use Azure SRE Agent to investigate incidents, identify root causes, and automate remediation. Leave with practical experience applying AI agents across the modernization and operations lifecycle.

Take a working agent that misses its target and improve it through hill climbing: a repeatable process for making one measured change at a time. embeddingContent: Improve token efficiency with vLLM Semantic Router In this lab, you'll build a single endpoint for multiple models on AMD Instinct™ GPUs and use vLLM Semantic Router to match each request to the right model. Route simple tasks to smaller models and complex work to larger ones to save tokens and compute, while keeping sensitive requests on trusted local models. Connect an agent, explore routing decisions, and put your skills to the test by building your own router in a short challenge.

Operate secure, multi-tenant agentic apps on Azure Container Apps

Build the skills to run multi-tenant isolated AI workloads in production. You will place a workload in the right isolation boundary for user separation, contain untrusted code, scale from zero, right size CPU and memory for per second billing, and snapshot and resume sessions so stateful work can continue. Everything runs on Azure Container Apps with microVM-backed compute. Leave with a decision tree and patterns you can apply to your own workloads.

Experience how Dynamics 365 Activate can help simplify the journey from SAP ECC to Dynamics 365. In this hands-on lab, connect to a provided SAP ECC test environment, assess the migration scope, configure mappings, and execute a trial migration. You'll experience the migration journey from initial discovery through validation, giving you a practical understanding of how to plan and prepare for an SAP ECC migration to Dynamics 365.

AI is changing how people work and how organizations build new business capabilities. Join Jacob Andreou, Executive Vice President, Copilot, to explore how Copilot brings asking, delegating, building, and scaling together, and how Windows extends that experience across the PC. Learn how Teams connects people, agents, and business processes across functions, and how new FinOps capabilities help organizations manage and scale Copilot with confidence. See what becomes possible when AI is built into the flow of work, from the individual to the organization.

Seating is limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis. We encourage you to arrive early to secure a seat before the session begins.

12,000 Seats. Six Months. A New Direction with Windows 365.

An EUC renewal can be more than a licensing decision — it can be the catalyst for a completely different approach.
This session follows a real-world, 12,000-seat renewal and the six-month migration journey that followed, with Windows 365 at the heart of the replacement strategy. We’ll explore why we chose it, how we approached the transition, and the practical decisions and trade-offs along the way.

embeddingContent:
Closing the AI Adoption Gap: Women Shaping What's Next

AI is transforming how we work, how companies operate, and the future of work. At the same time, research suggesting that women are adopting AI at a slower pace than men raises an important question: How do we ensure more women have the confidence, skills, and opportunities to shape what comes next? This panel brings together women working in AI today to share how they're driving innovation, empowering their teams and communities, and creating new opportunities for others to participate.

Panelists will share candid perspectives on the barriers that remain, practical approaches to closing the AI adoption gap, and actionable ideas to help more women move beyond using AI to influencing, building, and leading with it.

Many Domain Agents, One Governance Model: An Azure Pattern

Every business unit wants its own agent, and most platforms give each one its own identity, tool access and blind spots. This session traces a production multi-domain architecture end to end: one governed entry at the Azure API Management AI gateway, per-domain agents with scoped Entra Agent IDs, brokered tool access through governed MCP with content safety on tool-call arguments, and Foundry Control Plane across the fleet, all in the customer's own tenant.

embeddingContent: Monitoring without polling: Real-time, change-driven monitoring Modern observability collects telemetry in near real time, yet many monitoring workflows rely on periodic evaluation, adding latency and missing transient or absent conditions. This talk introduces change-driven monitoring, where continuous queries evaluate system state and trigger reactions as conditions change. Using Drasi, a Microsoft-backed CNCF Sandbox project, we’ll demonstrate detection of failures, stalled workflows, missing heartbeats, and SLO violations, with alerts and self-healing.

embeddingContent: All or nothing: Distributed transactions in Azure Cosmos DB What if 'all or nothing' just worked across your whole database? We'll live-code the classic move-money-and-place-order scenario, look at how two-phase commit works under the hood, and cover where it fits today. If you've been hand-rolling consistency, this one's for you.

In a live Fabric demonstration, we expose how broad schema selection, undefined business terms and weak examples make a data agent return plausible but wrong answers. Then we fix it: tighten the schema, improve the instructions, add example queries and rerun a fixed benchmark. The generated T-SQL stays on screen throughout. Leave able to test a Fabric data agent, measure improvement and defend the result to a business sponsor.

embeddingContent:
Confidently Wrong: What Bad Data Does to Good Agents

An agent running on bad data doesn't crash. It answers confidently, it's wrong, and somebody acts on it. Before two agents went live, we had to decide whether the data underneath could be trusted with a business decision: a heavy equipment onboarding agent, and a Microsoft Fabric modernization for a global energy operator. Neither was ready on day one. We'll show the governance work each one needed, what broke early, and a short checklist to run before you hand your next agent the keys.

ogDescription:

This session explains how to decide which controls need Deny from day one versus which stay Audit, using real governance patterns: a framework for deciding before go-live, not after a finding.

embeddingContent: Two Doors Out of SQL Server: Mirroring vs Change Event Streaming Not everyone's analytics estate lives in one platform. SQL Server 2025 gives you two exits: Mirroring, which lands current-state tables in OneLake, and Change Event Streaming, which pushes row-level change events to Event Hubs, where Fabric Eventstream or Azure Databricks Structured Streaming can pick them up. One is Fabric-native | the other is portable. We'll build the bronze medallion layer on both, and cover why you can only enable one per database.

embeddingContent:
Agent Cost Is an Architecture Decision, Not a Token Count

One agent serves 40,000 requests a month and costs 40 dollars. The next serves 9,000 and costs 1,440, which is 85% of the bill. Volume does not predict agent cost. Orchestration does. Agents are stateless, so a loop rereads its whole history and input grows quadratically | ten steps bill 42,500 tokens against a naive 20,000. We derive that math on stage, price it live against public cloud pricing APIs, and find the cascade break even that flips a saving into an overspend. Code included.

Single-shot RAG breaks on hard questions: grab a few chunks, answer confidently anyway. In this 25-minute hands-on session, go deep on agentic retrieval on Azure Cosmos DB. The Cosmos DB MCP Toolkit makes retrieval a first-class agent tool — iterative, multi-hop RAG that detects gaps, issues follow-up sub-queries, and synthesizes a grounded answer. Then wire an agent to hosted MCP (preview), secured with Entra ID, to reach live Cosmos data with nothing to deploy. We build it live, hop by hop.

embeddingContent:
Building multi-agent AI apps on Azure Cosmos DB

Building a multi-agent AI system? The hard part isn't the agents — it's the data layer underneath. In this 45-minute table talk, let's compare how we handle memory, conversation history, shared state, and retrieval when many agents run at once. We'll debate short- vs long-term memory, isolating each agent's context while sharing world state, grounding agents in live data, and scaling to thousands of sessions. Bring your architecture and questions and share ideas with the Cosmos DB team.

embeddingContent:
Partition keys, unlocked: Evolving data models in Azure Cosmos DB

The old rule — 'get your partition key perfect on day one, or rewrite' — is dead. In this discussion, let's rethink data modeling on Azure Cosmos DB. Where should enterprise AI run: device, edge, cloud, or everywhere? Rockwell Automation argues for a hybrid, distributed model that places each workload by latency, data sensitivity, compute needs, resilience, and cost. Learn a six-step placement rule and a Cloud → Edge → Device architecture. Execute AI as close to the source as practical, and as centrally as necessary. "AI everywhere" is the destination; workload placement is the design decision.

Agent 365: Governing agent access to Microsoft 365 content

embeddingContent: AI-scale growth: How Hugging Face and Instacart scale in-memory data AI companies can experience rapid growth that places new demands on in-memory data infrastructure, from thread bottlenecks and resharding to tail latency and backup memory use. Explore how two teams address these challenges. Hugging Face split its Redis setup as the Hub reached 3 million models, then adopted Dragonfly to simplify operations. Instacart replaced 348 ElastiCache nodes with 100 Dragonfly nodes and reduced average and P99 latency by 40–50%, with no customer impact.

embeddingContent: Guardrails and governance strike back An AI agent can stay within every permission, touch only allowed data, pass every security check and still potentially cause harm. Cut through the noise around agentic guardrails and governance with two anchors: Can vs. Should, which asks whether an agent’s next action makes sense beyond permission; and Point-in-Time vs. the Chain, which shows how risk can emerge across a sequence of individually reasonable actions. Learn how to question governance claims and build more effective controls.

embeddingContent: Know when AI should yield to human judgment AI has become remarkably capable at analysis, correlation, recommendation, and prediction. Yet the closer AI gets to decisions with real operational consequences, the more administrators insist on human authority in the final dispatch. Using 2026 survey data from more than 1,000 sysadmins, this session examines where that boundary exists, why it persists, and what it tells us about the future of autonomous IT.

Same software and APIs as on-premises, so teams can move AI from experiments to production.

Your apps are down. What comes back first? When Exchange, SharePoint, and Teams go down together, most IT teams have backup, but no plan for what comes back first. Rubrik heard this everywhere, including from Simpson Strong-Tie: nobody had defined critical people in advance, so recovery got improvised, costing days.
In this fireside, Varun Grover and Mohammad Akram cover Autonomous Business Recovery: restoring the Minimum Viable Company first. Recovery that took 7-10 days now lands under 3 hours.
